Notes: User-reviewed Dameli etymology, 2026-09-09, batch 3. Possible Nuristani borrowing; donor unidentified. CDIAL groups Dameli zâdi under hā́rdi and notes irregular -d- < -rd-. Halfmann (2022), Advances in the historical phonology of the Nuristani languages, pp. 126–129 (especially p. 129), compares Dameli zādī with Ashkun židī́ heart: PII *-r̥d- > d in both, unlike other Nuristani languages; compare Nuristani Kalasha zö, Prasun zir, OIA hr̥daya and Avestan zərəδaya. Halfmann leaves three explanations open: borrowing from an earlier stage of a known Nuristani language, borrowing from an extinct Nuristani language, or Nuristani genealogical affiliation of Dameli. Ashkun is a comparandum, not an identified donor. Retain CDIAL 14064 as the provisional family index, not a claim of secure direct Indo-Aryan inheritance or a resolution of hā́rdi versus hr̥daya formation. The possible borrowing is recorded in Notes because the lab has no uncertain-borrowing Kind. Research source: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368760201_Advances_in_the_historical_phonology_of_the_Nuristani_languages .
